t: For the purposes of section 504 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 414), appropriated funds available to an intelligence agency may be obligated or expended for an intelligence or intelligence-related activity as appropriated for fiscal year 2010, as modified by such reprogramming and transfers of funds authorized by and reported to the appropriate congressional committees.

fable.w: The section only addresses when appropriated funds may be obligated or expended by an intelligence agency, with reprogramming reported to congressional committees. The tempting reading is that reporting to committees is a form of consultation, but Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. No outside party (states, the public, experts, companies) is involved in any federal decision here.
fable.s: reprogramming and transfers of funds authorized by and reported to the appropriate congressional committees

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the expenditure of funds by an intelligence agency, subject to reporting requirements to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is internal coordination, not participation by outside parties. There is no mention of consultation with states, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: appropriated funds available to an intelligence agency may be obligated or expended for an intelligence or intelligence-related activity as appropriated for fiscal year 2010, as modified by such reprogramming and transfers of funds authorized by and reported to the appropriate congressional committees.

opus.w: This section only allows appropriated intelligence funds to be spent, as adjusted by reprogrammings and transfers. The only interaction it describes is reporting to congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so this is not participation. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no one is given a right to sue.
opus.s: as modified by such reprogramming and transfers of funds authorized by and reported to the appropriate congressional committees

qwen_chat.w: The section requires that fund reprogramming and transfers be reported to congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this reporting requirement is an internal government procedure and does not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: as modified by such reprogramming and transfers of funds authorized by and reported to the appropriate congressional committees.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that reporting to congressional committees constitutes "participation" because Congress is involved in the oversight process. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to them is intra-governmental coordination/oversight, not participation by an outside party.
